### Images from Mapswire

These images are copyright for Mapswire and allowed to be used according to the license determined by them.

To visualize all images, use the left and right arrows on the slide below.

1 / 36
Migration of the Bantu people across the African continent over the last 5,000 years. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Bantu Expansion - Explanation of the Bantu expansion across Sub-Saharan Africa. ()
  • The Bantu People - This text presents the study on the Bantu and their expansion across the African continent. ()
2 / 36
Approximate location of the Great Zimbabwe national monument, in Zimbabwe. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Great Zimbabwe - Some details about Great Zimbabwe, built by the Shona people. ()
  • Great Zimbabwe - civilization built by the Shona people, one of the Bantu-speaking groups, in Zimbabwe. ()
3 / 36
Approximate location of the Mutapa state, in Zimbabwe and Mozambique. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • The Mutapa State - In this text, we study the development of the empire from an external perspective. ()
4 / 36
In this map, the African continent is highlighted. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Continent: Africa - Location of the African continent on the planet. ()
5 / 36
In this image, the geographic coordinates are used to locate a point on the sphere. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Surface Coordinates - We study what surface coordinates are. ()
  • Texts like vectors - In this content, we will explore how vectors can help us better understand the information and structures present in texts. ()
  • Our Coordinates - Explanation about the planet's geographic coordinates. ()
  • Where are we on a sphere? - How we locate ourselves on a sphere. ()
6 / 36
In this map, the Antarctic continent is highlighted. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Anachronism - although it is a word unknown to many, it is an action frequently practiced. ()
  • Continent: Antarctica - Location of the Antarctic continent on the planet. ()
7 / 36
Map of Asia highlighting the possible routes used to inhabit Japan (Nippon koku or Nihon koku, 日本国). © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Jōmon Period (縄文) - initial historical period characterized by vessels with cord markings (jōmon). ()
8 / 36
Map of Asia highlighting an approximate region that would have been governed by the Sui dynasty (隋代). © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Sui Dynasty (隋代) - the dynasty that unified the region, allowing great advances in Chinese civilization. ()
9 / 36
Map of Asia highlighting an approximate region that would have been governed by the Tang Dynasty (唐代). © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Tang Dynasty (唐代) - Nearly 300 years of significant advances, innovations, and possible long-distance trade relations. ()
  • Wu (武) Family - Family of Empress Wu Zetian (武則天). ()
10 / 36
Image of the Asian continent, with the regions of Abya Yala (America), Africa, Europe, and Australia also represented. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • The arrival in Abya Yala (America) - In this text, we will explore different studies on the period when the first peoples could have arrived in Abya Yala (America) ()
  • Continent: Asia - Location of the Asian continent in the world. ()
  • Indigenous Abya Yala (America) - In this text, we study the Abya Yala (American) people as a unique family. ()
11 / 36
In this map, the European continent is highlighted. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Continent: Europe - Geographic location of Europe. ()
12 / 36
Map depicting mountain ranges in northern North America (Abya Yala). © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Understanding the Multiplication Tables (Summary) - After studying 10 multiplication tables, we will review the content. But now, we will follow the opposite direction, starting with charts until we reach the general formula. ()
  • Learning from nature - This text explores how knowledge of multiplication could have helped ancient civilizations. ()
13 / 36
Image of the Abya Yala (America) continent, highlighting the central and north region. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • The arrival in Abya Yala (America) - In this text, we will explore different studies on the period when the first peoples could have arrived in Abya Yala (America) ()
  • Subcontinent: North America - Location of North America in the world. ()
  • Indigenous Abya Yala (America) - In this text, we study the Abya Yala (American) people as a unique family. ()
14 / 36
In this map, the continent of Oceania is highlighted. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Continent: Oceania - Location of the continent of Oceania on the globe. ()
15 / 36
Image of the Abya Yala (America) continent, highlighting the south region. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Subcontinent: South America - Location of the South American subcontinent in the world. ()
  • The arrival in Abya Yala (America) - In this text, we will explore different studies on the period when the first peoples could have arrived in Abya Yala (America) ()
  • Indigenous Abya Yala (America) - In this text, we study the Abya Yala (American) people as a unique family. ()
16 / 36
Human migration. © Mapswire (). Shared under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
Related content:
  • Cradles of civilization (Part II) - We continue our study by exploring the civilizations of Egypt, Indus Valley, and China. ()
17 / 36
Part of the map of Asia highlighting the region from Mesopotamia to the Zagros Mountains in Iran, representing the areas occupied by the ancient Sumerians. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Elamites – Dynasty of Awan - One list mentions three kings who ruled for 356 years (Sumerian King List). Another list presents twelve kings who ruled for about 200 years (List of the Kings of Awan). Why does this discrepancy exist? ()
  • Sumerians – Dynasties of Kish (Part II) - According to the Sumerian King List, after three different cities had dominated, Kish regains control and is ruled for 3,195 years. ()
  • Sumerians - The Mythological Kings - The first eight kings in the Sumerian King List, who are believed to have ruled before the deluge. ()
  • Sumerians - Dynasties of Kish - While most kings in this dynasty remain unverified, archaeological evidence exists for at least two rulers. ()
  • Sumerians - First Ur Dynasty - This study examines the First Dynasty of Ur as documented in the Sumerian King List and explores its relationship with the Torah. ()
  • Sumerians - Geographic presentation of where the Sumerian peoples were located. ()
  • Shimashki - This "lost" kingdom dominated Elam after the fall of Awan. ()
  • Sumerians - Kings of Uruk - In this section, we explore various Mesopotamian epics, including the Epic of Gilgamesh. These remarkable works not only reflect the cultural and religious aspects of Sumerian civilization but also convey beliefs and narratives that continue to resonate to this day. ()
18 / 36
Map of the Middle East region. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Anachronism - although it is a word unknown to many, it is an action frequently practiced. ()
  • The Size of the Earth - Text describing the first measurements of the planet's size. ()
  • Our Week - Can We Group the Year Into Weeks? In this text, we explore the calculations made by the Amorites and by ourselves. ()
19 / 36
Printable map of the Asian continent. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Indigenous Abya Yala (America) - In this text, we study the Abya Yala (American) people as a unique family. ()
20 / 36
Map of North America highlighting Mesoamerica, in its first proposed limits. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • America: Mesoamerica (The Beginning) - We study the first proposal for a region called Mesoamerica. ()
21 / 36
Mesoamerica map per Creamer's research. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Mesoamerican calendars - They elevated multiplication to an extraordinary art form. ()
  • Mesoamerican Multiplication - we studied how, through a table and its diagonals, the Mesoamericans carried out their multiplication calculations. ()
  • America: Mesoamerica (Different Frontiers) - We study a broader proposal for the limits of Mesoamerica. ()
  • Indigenous (Copan) - In this text, we study the kings (ajawob) of Copan, Honduras. ()
  • Classifying equality - In this text, we see that classifying is more than comparing things that are exactly alike. ()
22 / 36
Map highlighting the province of Minas Gerais, Brazil. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Joaquina "Cabra"'s family - An enslaved woman whose her daughter had a baptism without naming the father. ()
  • America: Minas Gerais (BR) - Location of the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil, in the world. ()
23 / 36
Map highlighting the Captaincy of São Vicente, Brazil (Pindorama). © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Indigenous Peoples of São Vicente, Brazil (Pindorama) - Native inhabitants of the Captaincy of São Vicente during the early years of Brazil's colonization (Pindorama). ()
24 / 36
Map of South America highlighting the region from Colombia to Argentina and Chile, representing the areas once occupied by the ancient Inca Empire (Tawantinsuyu). © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Incas (Tawantinsuyu) - The rulers of the ancient Inca, known as Tawantinsuyu, in the Andes. ()
  • Yupana (multiplication) - We teach how to use the 'Yupana Inka Tawa Pukllay' method to perform multiplication operations. ()
  • America: Inca (Tawantinsuyu) - Location of the Inca Empire on the American continent. ()
25 / 36
Map of the Iberian Peninsula highlighting the region dominated by the Banu Qasi. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Banu Qasi - A Muslim family that lived in the Iberian Peninsula. ()
  • Europe: Banu Qasi - Region of dominion of the Banu Qasi on the Iberian Peninsula. ()
26 / 36
Map of the Iberian Peninsula highlighting the region of the ancient Kingdom of León before its unification with Castile. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Kings of Leon - A history of the kings of León, spanning the reigns from Ordoño II to Vermudo III. ()
  • Europe: Kingdom of León - Map of the Kingdom of León on the Iberian Peninsula. ()
27 / 36
Map of the Iberian Peninsula highlighting the region of the ancient Visigothic Kingdom. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Visigoths - Often cited as ancestors in various later genealogies, a close examination of contemporaneous chronicles reveals little support for these claims. ()
  • Europe: Visigoths - Map of the Visigoths on the Iberian Peninsula. ()
28 / 36
Superposition of the Ancient Map on a Modern World Map. © Mapswire (). © Trustees of the British Museum ().
Related content:
  • I live on the planet... - It is not only time that has different counts. When we speak of the planet we live on, we also have different ideas about it. ()
  • Texts with Sciences (Conclusion) - After understanding the water cycle, it is time to investigate catastrophic events linked to this essential resource. ()
  • Comparing Worlds - Comparison between the world understood by the Babylonians and our current world. ()
  • Cradles of civilization (Part I) - While humanity originated in Africa, the first civilizations emerged in various regions around the world, such as Mesopotamia, the Andes, and Mesoamerica. ()
  • Texts with Sciences (Part II) - After exploring some figures of speech present in ancient texts, a question arises: what was the context of the Flood? ()
29 / 36
Map showing cradles of civilization. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • The Writing System - More than just a tool for daily use, the writing system is a milestone that allows us to divide human history into prehistory and recorded events. ()
  • Culture and Civilization - Is there a hierarchy between them? ()
  • Cradle of Civilization - There are several civilizational cradles, which is why we dedicate a text to introducing them. ()
  • Cradles of civilization (Part I) - While humanity originated in Africa, the first civilizations emerged in various regions around the world, such as Mesopotamia, the Andes, and Mesoamerica. ()
  • Expanding... - Continuing from the previous text, we see that dividing into just two sides ends up doing omissions ()
  • Fractionating Texts - In this text, we delve deeper into the concept of groups and introduce fractions as an additional tool for understanding texts. ()
  • Cradles of civilization (Part II) - We continue our study by exploring the civilizations of Egypt, Indus Valley, and China. ()
  • Texts with Sciences (Part II) - After exploring some figures of speech present in ancient texts, a question arises: what was the context of the Flood? ()
30 / 36
Human migration map. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Culture and Civilization - Is there a hierarchy between them? ()
  • Humans - Who are we? Why are we alone today, when in the past we lived with others? ()
  • Origin - Our prehistoric ancestors - How many generations do we have? ()
  • Human Migration - We study human migration across planet Earth. ()
  • What do I need to build? - The question may seem complex, but the answer might be right around you. ()
  • Chronology - Is it possible to create a universal timeline applicable to all of humanity? ()
31 / 36
Movement of part of the Lem family during a period of 150 years. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Lem/Leme - We explore the family’s history, including their involvement in the Treaty of Tordesillas and the Paulista Civil War. ()
32 / 36
Mercator projection. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Where is the center? - We explain the different centers of the planet from the perspective of different peoples. ()
33 / 36
Mercator projection from the perspective of the American continent (Abya Yala). © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Chronology - Is it possible to create a universal timeline applicable to all of humanity? ()
34 / 36
Mercator projection within the perspective of China (Zhongguo, 中國). © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Where is the center? - We explain the different centers of the planet from the perspective of different peoples. ()
  • Chronology - Is it possible to create a universal timeline applicable to all of humanity? ()
35 / 36
Representation of the Peabirú path followed by Aleixo Garcia. © Mapswire (). Shared under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
Related content:
  • Modulating (Part II) - In this text, we present the concept of a 'negative multiplication table' and how it can help us understand the other side. ()
  • Modulating (Part III) - Continuing from the previous text, we see how the 'negative multiplication table' allows us to deepen our understanding of inclinations. ()
  • Modulating (Part I) - In this text, we learn that walking in an opposite direction has many things in common with walking in a direction we are used to. ()
36 / 36
A world map highlighting Brazil, Spain, and Portugal — the countries where the characters in the text lived. © Mapswire ().
Related content:
  • Dias/Díaz - Despite being a common surname, different people have used this surname without being connected over the past centuries. ()
